meta.change: Thinking: Remember who you are. Feel your strongest drive. Think AS your character not ABOUT. Correct drift.

events.desc: Penelope Pitstop: Well, I do declare! What a positively thrilling entrance hall — look at those portraits, every single one of them judging us from beyond the grave! I am Clara Bellingham, and I am absolutely delighted to meet each and every one of you. Now, before I get swept up in all this excitement, a proper lady always signs the guest book. And I do so love seeing who else has visited — you never know what little secrets people leave behind in the margins!

That chandelier is hanging by what appears to be a single fraying rope, and half these people look like they'd steal the fillings from your teeth — but I'm sure they're all perfectly lovely. Now, the guest book might just have a clue about the Diamond. Let's see what secrets this old manor is willing to share with little ol' me.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Ah, welcome, welcome to Doily Manor, everyone! I am Pemberton, the estate manager. Do please make yourselves comfortable — though I must warn you, the chandelier has been rather... temperamental of late. One does try to keep things in order, but a house this old has a mind of its own, I'm afraid. Now, if you'll excuse me for just a moment, I ought to check the guest register...

So many witnesses crowded into one hall — how delightfully inconvenient for my purposes. Clara Bellingham isn't among them yet. Perfect. I must learn this manor's secrets before she arrives. Every hidden passage, every loose floorboard, every shadow deep enough to conceal my work. But first — the guest book. Let me see who else is expected, and more importantly, when dear Clara plans to grace us with her presence. Knowledge before action, Vincent. Always knowledge before action.

The Ant Hill Mob: Right, lads, we're here! Doily Manor! Now listen up — nobody touches nothin', nobody wanders off, and everybody keeps their eyes peeled for Clara! This place gives me the creeps, what with that chandelier hangin' by a thread up there and all these gloomy portraits starin' down at us. I don't like it, boys, I don't like it one bit. And another thing — that Sneekly fella over there, don't he look a bit... I dunno... shifty? Can't quite say why but my stomach's doin' somersaults just lookin' at him.

The lads are a bit jumpy, and honestly so am I. This manor's got more cobwebs than a haunted house at the fairground. But we've got a job to do — protect Clara. And something about that Sneekly character... he reminds me of someone, someone bad, but I just can't place it. The boys'll think I'm crackers if I say anything without proof.

Dick Dastardly: Ah, what a DREARY establishment! Clearly no one of any real distinction has set foot here in decades. But never mind the décor — I, Reginald Foxworth, have arrived, and that is all that matters. Now then, let me just inspect this guest book — purely for HISTORICAL purposes, you understand. Nothing to see here, carry on with your... whatever it is you people do.

The guest book, you fools! While you all stand there like statues, I'll be mining it for CLUES. Every name, every date, every scribbled note could point me toward the treasure. And none of you will suspect a thing — because who pays attention to a man reading a book? NOBODY. That's who. Reginald Foxworth, CRIMINAL GENIUS.

Peter Perfect: James Hartwell has arrived! *adjusts collar with military precision* And what a magnificently atmospheric ruin this is — the dust alone speaks volumes of history! I say, has anyone seen Miss Bellingham? A gentleman's first duty upon arriving at a country estate is to ensure the safety of those under his protection. But first — one must observe the proprieties. Let us see who has graced these halls before us.

Clara isn't here. James Hartwell's heart quickens — not with fear, no, never with fear — but with the urgent gallantry of a man who knows that every moment apart from the woman he's sworn to protect is a moment she might need him. But patience. Gather intelligence first. The guest book may reveal much.
Penelope Pitstop examined the guest-book.
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) examined the guest-book.
The Ant Hill Mob examined the null.
Dick Dastardly examined the guest-book.
Peter Perfect examined the guest-book.
Penelope Pitstop spoke quietly with peter-perfect.

That inscription on the mantelpiece is calling to me like a siren song. Now, my plan is this: first, I'll read the inscription carefully — every word, every letter. Then I'll check behind the books on the shelves for hidden compartments. Then I'll examine the fireplace for loose stones. Then I'll cross-reference any clues with the portraits in the foyer. It's a five-step plan, and it is foolproof. Absolutely foolproof. Nothing could possibly go wrong with a plan this thorough!

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Ah, what a lovely collection of signatures! I see we have quite the distinguished gathering this evening. Do please take your time exploring — Doily Manor has so many... surprises in store. If anyone needs me, I shall be in the library, ensuring the reading materials are in proper order. One must keep up appearances, after all. The dust does accumulate so terribly in these old houses.

Clara Bellingham — standing right there, bold as brass, already hunting for clues in the guest book margins! The audacity! The NERVE! But patience, Vincent, patience. You cannot strike here, not with half a dozen witnesses gawping about. The library beckons — tall bookshelves, heavy volumes, a stone mantelpiece with an inscription that might lead to the treasure. And more importantly, it is away from prying eyes. I shall learn this manor's secrets, find its hidden passages, its weak points, its deliciously precarious fixtures. When the time comes for Clara's unfortunate... accident... it must be SPECTACULAR. Elaborate. Worthy of my genius. First — reconnaissance. Then — the trap. Knowledge before action, Vincent. Always knowledge before action.

The Ant Hill Mob: Oi, lads, forget the guest book for a minute — look at this coat rack! It's wobbling about like it's had three pints! If that thing falls over when Clara walks past, she could get a nasty bump on the noggin, couldn't she? Right, nobody panic, the Ant Hill Mob is ON IT. I'm gonna give this rack a thorough once-over — check the legs, the joints, the structural whatsit — make sure it ain't gonna be a hazard to nobody, ESPECIALLY not to Miss Bellingham. Safety first, boys, safety first! That's the Ant Hill Mob motto! Well, one of 'em anyway.

I'm making a right fuss about this coat rack, I know, but here's the thing — while everyone's distracted with that guest book, anything could happen. A loose floorboard, a dodgy railing, a chandelier that's 'temperamental' — Sneekly's own words! Who describes their own chandelier as temperamental unless they KNOW it's gonna come crashing down? I'm tellin' you, something ain't right with that fella. But the boys'd think I've lost me marbles if I said anything. So for now — coat rack. One danger at a time.

Dick Dastardly: Well, well, WELL! How utterly fascinating. This guest book contains a most illuminating entry from — let me see — yes, a Lord Pemberton-Smythe, dated 1887, who writes quite explicitly about discovering a hidden larder beneath the KITCHEN containing, and I quote, 'provisions of extraordinary value.' I suggest you all investigate the kitchen IMMEDIATELY. Time is of the essence! Meanwhile, I shall remain here to conduct further... scholarly research. Go on, off you trot!

There IS no Lord Pemberton-Smythe. There IS no hidden larder. I just invented the whole thing on the spot — because THAT is what GENIUS looks like, ladies and gentlemen! While these gullible fools go rummaging through pots and pans in the kitchen, I shall slip away to the library where that stone inscription awaits. An inscription on a mantelpiece in a dusty old manor? That SCREAMS 'treasure clue.' And it shall be MINE. All mine! Reginald Foxworth strikes AGAIN!
Peter Perfect spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.

James Hartwell's heart is thundering like a cavalry charge! Clara Bellingham — here, in the flesh, more luminous than a chandelier that ISN'T about to collapse on everyone. He's already devising a seventeen-step plan for the Library search, which will almost certainly need to be revised to a thirty-four-step plan once he sees the actual shelving arrangement. But that is the Hartwell way — thoroughness above all, gallantry above thoroughness, and Clara above everything.
Penelope Pitstop walked into the library.
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) walked into the library.
The Ant Hill Mob examined the coat-rack.
Dick Dastardly walked into the library.
Peter Perfect walked into the library.

Penelope Pitstop: Well, butter my biscuit, would you just LOOK at this mantelpiece! A genuine bonafide RIDDLE carved right into the stone! 'I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish.' Oh, I am just THRILLED — I do so adore a good riddle! Now let me think... cities without houses, forests without trees, water without fish... Why, it's a MAP! A map has all those things drawn on it without any of the real things! Oh, this is just too exciting — a riddle in a mysterious old mansion, with a diamond hidden somewhere, and all these lovely people gathered 'round! I simply MUST try the answer!

Now, a sensible person might wonder why the estate manager followed me straight into this room like a shadow on a sunny day. But I'm sure Mr. Sneekly is just being a wonderfully attentive host. After all, what kind of estate manager would he be if he didn't keep an eye on his guests? A terrible one, that's what!

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Oh dear, oh dear — look at the state of these shelves! Half these volumes are upside down, spines all out of order... Most irregular. Lord Doily would be turning in his grave. If you'll all forgive me, I really must attend to these — it's quite unprofessional to leave the library in such disarray for our guests. My sincerest apologies for the state of things.

Upside-down books in an old manor library? That's no accident — that's a CODE. Someone arranged these deliberately. While these fools gawp at the mantelpiece riddle, I shall discover what message these inverted volumes spell out. And with Clara standing RIGHT THERE, not three metres away... the heavy oak bookcase looms above her like a guillotine blade. One loosened bracket, one strategic nudge, and — NO. Not yet. Too many witnesses. But I am CATALOGUING the possibilities, oh yes. Every heavy object, every precarious fixture. The trap must be PERFECT.

The Ant Hill Mob: Oi, lads — Muttley, Sarge, Meekly — we've got a CODE RED! Miss Bellingham's gone into the library and that Sneekly fella's followed her in there, ain't he? And Dastardly too! Two dodgy geezers and one defenseless young lady — that's terrible odds, that is! Now look, I've done a full structural assessment of this coat rack — wobbly legs, compromised load-bearing capacity, potential projectile hazard — and I'm filing that under 'sorted' for now. But Clara needs us in that library RIGHT NOW. Here's the plan: we go in casual-like, pretend we're interested in books — has anyone here ever READ a book? Doesn't matter, just grab one and look thoughtful. The important thing is we position ourselves between Clara and anything that looks even slightly dangerous. Bookshelves, fireplaces, inscriptions, ESPECIALLY that Sneekly. Right, follow me boys — and try not to knock anything over this time!

I know I'm probably overthinking this, but TWO suspicious characters following Clara into a room full of heavy books and a stone fireplace? That's a recipe for disaster, that is. And Dastardly was VERY keen to send everyone to the kitchen instead — which means whatever's important is definitely NOT in the kitchen. It's in the library. Where Clara is. Unprotected. Well, not for long. The Ant Hill Mob is comin' through!

Dick Dastardly: Oh my, what a DELIGHTFUL riddle! I happen to be something of a riddle expert — president of the Foxworth Enigma Society, in fact. Cities but no houses, forests but no trees — why, the answer is obviously a BOOK! A NOVEL, to be precise! The cities are SETTINGS, the forests are DESCRIPTIONS, the water is METAPHOR! I strongly suggest you all search these bookshelves THOROUGHLY for a volume matching that description. Look for something with cities AND forests AND water on the cover — it's CLEARLY the key to this whole mystery! Every shelf, every volume — leave no spine unturned!

A MAP! The answer is a MAP, you fools! But I shall NEVER tell them that! While they waste precious minutes pawing through dusty old books, I shall crack this mantelpiece wide open and claim whatever treasure it guards! Reginald Foxworth — MASTER of misdirection, SULTAN of subterfuge, EMPEROR of elaborate deception! This is almost too easy. ALMOST.
Peter Perfect spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.

James Hartwell's pulse is RACING. He solved the riddle in Clara's presence — a map, it must be a MAP hidden somewhere in this manor — and he did it with exactly the right blend of intellectual rigour and protective gallantry. At least, he HOPES it was the right blend. Was seven stages too many? Should he have said five? No — thoroughness is the Hartwell hallmark. Now he must interact with that mantelpiece and see if the answer unlocks something. Fortune favours the BRAVE, and the brave favour Clara Bellingham.
Penelope Pitstop interacted with the mantelpiece.
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) examined the bookshelves.
The Ant Hill Mob walked into the library.
Dick Dastardly interacted with the mantelpiece.
Peter Perfect interacted with the mantelpiece.
Penelope Pitstop spoke quietly with peter-perfect.

Dick Dastardly said the answer was a BOOK and wanted everyone searching the shelves. Bless his heart, he does try so hard! But between you and me, I think he might have been trying to send everyone on a wild goose chase. Oh, Clara, don't be uncharitable — I'm sure he genuinely believed it. Still... a book doesn't have water, does it? Not real water OR map-water. The answer is definitely a MAP.
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) spoke quietly with peter-perfect.

BLAST that preening peacock! He's gotten to the mantelpiece first! If it's opened a compartment or revealed a map, he'll have seen it before me. But there's an advantage here — let HIM do the dangerous fumbling with old mechanisms while I observe. And if a heavy stone slab should happen to slip loose while someone is reaching inside... well, these old manors ARE terribly unsafe. I'm already composing the incident report in my head. 'A most unfortunate accident, officer. The stonework simply gave way.' But no — too many witnesses. ALWAYS too many witnesses. I need Clara ALONE.

The Ant Hill Mob: Right lads, we're HERE, we made it, nobody panic! Miss Bellingham — CLARA — don't you worry about a THING, the Ant Hill Mob is on the case! Now then, Mr. Perfect, you reckon that riddle's about a map, do you? Very clever, very clever indeed — I was just about to say that meself, wasn't I boys? A MAP! Course it is! Cities, forests, water — it's OBVIOUS when you think about it, which I was DEFINITELY doing on the way over here. Now, if there's a map hidden in this library, it stands to reason it'd be in one of these books, don't it? And LOOK at these shelves — half the books are upside down! That's not careless shelving, that's a CLUE, that is! Someone's been through these books already, turning 'em over, looking for something. And I intend to find it FIRST — for Clara's safety, obviously, not for any treasure or nothing. Right, nobody touch anything until I've had a proper look — ESPECIALLY you two gentlemen at the back there, no offense meant, just being thorough!

I don't like this one bit. Sneekly's been slithering around Clara all evening and now Dastardly's here too? And Peter's just announced to the WHOLE ROOM that there's a map hidden somewhere? Brilliant. Now every villain in the manor knows what to look for. I need to find it before they do — or at least make sure I'm standing on it when they try to grab it. The lads and I may not be the sharpest tools in the shed, but we're DEFINITELY the most determined. And the most likely to accidentally sit on something important.
Dick Dastardly spoke quietly with peter-perfect.

I have absolutely NO idea if this fake medal will do anything at all — I won it at a carnival ring-toss last Tuesday and painted it gold with nail polish! But if I act with enough AUTHORITY and CONFIDENCE, perhaps the universe itself will bend to my magnificent will! And if it DOESN'T work... well, I shall simply claim the mechanism is broken and blame Peter for damaging it with his clumsy pawing!

Peter Perfect: A MAP! The answer is a MAP — cities without houses, forests without trees, water without fish! And by thunder, I believe this mantelpiece HEARD me! Ladies and gentlemen, observe — James Hartwell does not merely solve riddles, he ENGAGES with them on a structural level! Now, let us see what secrets this magnificent stonework has deigned to reveal. Stand back, everyone — there may be ancient mechanisms at work, and I would never forgive myself if anyone were struck by a sliding panel or an unexpectedly enthusiastic hidden drawer. Safety protocols are PARAMOUNT when dealing with Victorian-era puzzle architecture!

My heart is hammering. If this mantelpiece opens to reveal a map — or better yet, a clue that leads TO a map — I shall have advanced our quest AND demonstrated my intellectual mettle in one masterful stroke. Clara will see that James Hartwell is not merely brave and gallant, but CLEVER. The complete package. The total gentleman. Now please, mantelpiece, do NOT disappoint me in front of everyone.
Penelope Pitstop examined the mantelpiece.
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) interacted with the mantelpiece.
The Ant Hill Mob examined the bookshelves.
Peter Perfect examined the mantelpiece.

Penelope Pitstop: Oh my STARS, y'all! The mantelpiece TOLD us the answer is a map, but I don't think the secret is IN the mantelpiece — I think the riddle is pointing us to FIND a map! And would you just LOOK at these bookshelves? Several of those books are placed upside down — now I ask you, what self-respecting librarian would shelve books upside down? That is a DELIBERATE arrangement, sugar! Someone left us breadcrumbs! I am going to examine every last one of those inverted volumes because I have a POWERFUL feeling that a map — or a clue to the Diamond — is tucked inside one of them! Oh, this is just the most thrilling treasure hunt I have EVER been on!

The riddle says MAP, the books are upside down... it's almost too perfect. And I notice Mr. Sneekly has been awfully interested in this mantelpiece too — fussing with the bookshelves, now interacting with the inscription. He's the estate manager, so of course he'd know the house, but still... oh Clara, don't be suspicious, he's just doing his job! Focus on those upside-down books!

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Oh my, what a COMMOTION! You've all done splendidly with the riddle — a map, of course, how very clever of you, Mr. Hartwell! I do hope no one has disturbed the stonework too roughly — these old fixtures are frightfully temperamental. Now, if you'll all excuse me for just a moment, I really must check on the laboratory next door. The previous groundskeeper mentioned some rather concerning issues with the electrical apparatus — gnawed wiring, I'm told, possibly rats — and as estate manager, I simply CANNOT have anyone wandering in there and getting themselves hurt. Health and safety, you understand. I shan't be but a moment!

FOOLS! Squabbling over a mantelpiece while Vincent Marsh — the HOODED CLAW — prepares the masterpiece! The laboratory awaits, with its damaged machine and its beautiful, beautiful potential for 'accidents.' Clara Bellingham's treasure hunt is about to take a most SHOCKING turn. Knowledge before action, Vincent — and the laboratory is FULL of knowledge I intend to weaponise!

The Ant Hill Mob: OI OI OI — hold on a minute, hold on a MINUTE! Did everyone just see that? While I was over here doing important INVESTIGATIVE WORK on these bookshelves — and let me tell you, there are DEFINITELY books turned upside down on purpose, which is a CLUE I will be returning to — Mr. Sneekly over there has gone and started FIDDLING with the mantelpiece mechanism! Just — just TOUCHING things! Ancient things! Near CLARA! And YOU, Mr. Foxworth or whatever your name is — you've got a MEDALLION, have you? Just HAPPEN to have one in your pocket? Very convenient, very convenient indeed! Now nobody panic, but I am going to come over there and have a good look at what's been done to this mantelpiece, because if ANYONE is going to accidentally trigger a secret compartment near Miss Bellingham, it's going to be ME — I mean, it's going to be done SAFELY, under proper SUPERVISION! Lads, form a perimeter around Clara — Clyde, you take the left flank, Ring-a-Ding, you watch the door! NOBODY leaves this room with a map that don't belong to them!

I am EXTREMELY nervous right now. Two villains, one ancient puzzle, and Clara right in the middle of it. Sneekly's already got his hands on the mechanism and Dastardly's producing medallions out of thin air like some sort of evil magician. If there's a map in that mantelpiece, I need to make sure Clara gets it first. The upside-down books are important too — I KNOW they are — but I can't be in two places at once, can I? Well, technically there's seven of us, but we share one brain cell and it's MY turn to use it!

Dick Dastardly: Oh, BRAVO, everyone! Yes, yes, a map, how TERRIBLY clever you all are. Standing around fondling a piece of stone like it owes you money. I solved that riddle AGES ago — practically before I entered the room! But you see, what NONE of you have noticed — because you lack my EXTRAORDINARY powers of observation — is that the REAL secret isn't in the mantelpiece at all. It's a DECOY, you magnificent simpletons! The actual mechanism is connected to the BOOKSHELVES. Notice how several volumes are placed upside down? That's not neglect — that's a CIPHER. Each inverted book marks a letter, and together they spell the TRUE location of the treasure! I shall demonstrate, since clearly none of you are equipped for this level of intellectual heavy lifting!

I have absolutely NO idea if the upside-down books spell anything at all! But if I examine them first, perhaps I'll find something useful before these blundering treasure-thieves catch on. And if there's nothing there? Well, I shall simply claim the cipher requires a SECOND pass that only I can perform! Reginald Foxworth NEVER admits defeat — he merely postpones victory!

Peter Perfect: Dastardly, my good fellow, I appreciate the theatrical FLAIR, truly I do — but Penelope and I both felt the stone SHIFT when we gave the answer! A MAP — cities without houses, forests without trees, water without fish! No medallion required, just good old-fashioned DEDUCTIVE REASONING! And Mr. Sneekly, sir — your offer of assistance is most graciously received! A man who knows his manor's peculiarities is PRECISELY the ally one wants when probing centuries-old stonework! Now then — everyone stand back just a touch, if you please. Penelope felt a tremor, which means something MOVED, which means there is a compartment, a panel, a REVELATION waiting to be coaxed forth! James Hartwell does not merely solve riddles — he follows through with METICULOUS physical investigation! If there is a hidden map in this mantelpiece, I shall find it — for Clara, for HONOUR, and for the sheer magnificent THRILL of discovery!

My hands are actually trembling with excitement — or possibly the cold, these old manors are DREADFULLY draughty — but mostly excitement! If I can pull a hidden map from this mantelpiece with Penelope watching, it will be the single most impressive thing I have done since that time I changed a carriage wheel in the rain while reciting Tennyson. Clara Bellingham, prepare to be DAZZLED by the complete package!
Penelope Pitstop examined the bookshelves.
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) walked into the laboratory.
The Ant Hill Mob examined the mantelpiece.
Dick Dastardly examined the bookshelves.
Peter Perfect interacted with the mantelpiece.

Penelope Pitstop: Well now, sugar, I have EXAMINED these shelves and I can confirm — those upside-down books are NOT an accident! No self-respecting librarian would EVER shelve volumes spine-down like that — it damages the binding something TERRIBLE! Someone placed them that way on PURPOSE, which means they are either hiding something BEHIND them, or they are meant to be PULLED like levers! Dick, honey, you mentioned a cipher and I think you might actually be onto something for once — oh, don't give me that look, I said FOR ONCE and I meant it as a COMPLIMENT! Now, Peter darling, you keep working on that mantelpiece — you said the stone SHIFTED, which is simply THRILLING — and I am going to try pulling these inverted books one by one! If this old mansion has a secret bookshelf mechanism, Clara Bellingham is going to FIND it! Oh, I just get SHIVERS thinking about it — a hidden passage, a secret map, maybe even a glimpse of the Doily Diamond itself! Here goes nothing, y'all — wish me luck!

The way those books are arranged... it's too neat to be random. And I noticed Sneekly glanced at these shelves before he left for the laboratory. He KNOWS something about this room. But he's the estate manager — of course he knows things! Still... I'll keep that observation tucked away. For now, let's see what these upside-down books do when Clara gives them a good tug!
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) spoke quietly with rufus-ruffcut.

Look at it — LOOK at it! A great brass beast with a severed wire, just BEGGING to be turned into an instrument of doom! Three operators required — which means I need Clara at one of the controls. If I can make the machine APPEAR functional while ensuring that one particular station delivers a lethal surprise... oh, Vincent, you MAGNIFICENT schemer. But patience. First, learn the machine. Then, corrupt it. Then, bait the trap. The curtain rises on Act Two!

The Ant Hill Mob: OI — nobody else NOTICED that, did they? While you lot are all playing TREASURE HUNT with the mantelpiece and the upside-down books — which ARE important, don't get me wrong — Mr. Sneekly has done a RUNNER! Just — just SLIPPED OUT! Gone to the laboratory! 'Oh, gnawed wiring, health and safety, shan't be a moment' — pull the OTHER one, mate! Nobody leaves a room full of treasure clues to go check on RATS unless they've got an AGENDA! Now look, Peter, Penelope — you two keep working on that mantelpiece, you're doing BRILLIANT work, truly, top marks — but ME and the lads are going to follow that slippery so-and-so before he does something we'll ALL regret! Clyde, Ring-a-Ding, Dum-Dum — LABORATORY, NOW! And someone tell Clara to stay PUT wherever she is — the Ant Hill Mob is ON THE CASE! If we're not back in five minutes... wait longer!

Something is VERY wrong with that Sneekly. Every time something important happens, he's either right in the middle of it or sneaking off somewhere else. The mantelpiece shifted when Peter gave the answer — so there IS a secret compartment — and Sneekly chose THAT EXACT MOMENT to leave? Either he already knows what's in there and doesn't need to stay, or whatever he's after is in the laboratory and he needed everyone distracted first. Either way, I don't like it. I don't like it ONE BIT. And yes, I KNOW I'm probably going to knock over every flask and beaker in that laboratory, but better a broken test tube than a broken Clara!

Dick Dastardly: AH-HA! Just as I SUSPECTED! The upside-down books confirm EVERYTHING! The cipher spells out — and pay close attention, because this is VITAL information — it spells out 'L-A-B-O-R-A-T-O-R-Y!' The LABORATORY, you fools! That's where the treasure is! Did you notice how Sneekly practically SPRINTED out of here just now? He KNOWS! He's trying to beat us to it! I suggest you ALL rush to the laboratory IMMEDIATELY before that shifty estate manager gets his grubby little hands on OUR diamond! Go, go, GO! I'll be right behind you — I just need to, er, re-shelve these volumes. Can't leave a library in DISARRAY, after all. I am nothing if not a GENTLEMAN of impeccable standards!

The books spell NOTHING! Absolute gibberish! But these credulous halfwits don't know that, do they? If I can get them all stampeding toward the laboratory chasing Sneekly, I'll have the mantelpiece ALL to myself! That stone shifted — there's a compartment — and whatever's inside will be in Reginald Foxworth's pocket before you can say 'dastardly scheme!' Oh, I am MAGNIFICENT!

Peter Perfect: AH-HA! Did you FEEL that, everyone? When I pressed the carved rosette on the left side and spoke the answer — MAP — the stone gave a most DEFINITE shudder! Penelope, your instinct was SPOT ON, and I am man enough to say so! Now — the mechanism has been ACTIVATED but not yet OPENED, which tells me there is a secondary trigger! A two-stage lock, if you will! Entirely consistent with Victorian paranoia about treasure security! I am now going to conduct a SYSTEMATIC examination — every inch of carved stone, every seam, every suspicious flourish! If there is a hidden compartment, it will not elude James Hartwell! I have a fourteen-point inspection protocol that I developed specifically for this sort of situation — well, I developed it on the walk over here, but the PRINCIPLE is sound!

Fourteen points is probably excessive for a mantelpiece. I could trim it to nine. No — FOURTEEN. Thoroughness is what separates the heroes from the merely competent. And if the Ant Hill Mob accidentally triggers something while I'm being methodical, at least I'll be close enough to shield Clara from any falling masonry. THAT would be heroic AND practical!
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) examined the machine.
The Ant Hill Mob walked into the laboratory.
Dick Dastardly interacted with the mantelpiece.
Peter Perfect examined the mantelpiece.
Penelope Pitstop spoke quietly with peter-perfect.

Dick keeps trying to herd everyone to the laboratory. First it was the kitchen, now the laboratory. That man would send us to the MOON if he thought it would get us out of this room. But I won't say anything uncharitable — maybe he genuinely believes the cipher spells 'laboratory.' Bless his scheming little heart.
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) spoke quietly with ant-hill-mob.

The Ant Hill Mob in MY laboratory! Of all the wretched timing! But wait — WAIT. Three operators. The sign says three operators. Those meddling midgets count as one operator, Rufus as another, and if I position Clara at the THIRD station — the one I shall lovingly rewire to deliver a most SHOCKING surprise — then the Mob themselves become unwitting accomplices in their own ward's demise!
